result.title: Multimodal In-Context Learning with Explicit Rule Induction
result.summary: A central challenge in multimodal in-context learning (MICL) arises from tasks that are ill-defined without context and require uncovering the underlying rules from demonstrations. Existing methods predominantly treat MICL as direct input-output mapping, overlooking the importance of explicitly inducing and reasoning over such rules, limiting both performance and interpretability. We propose ERIM, Explicit Rule-Induction for Multimodal In-Context Learning, a unified framework that enhances MICL by explicitly inducing the latent rules governing demonstration samples. Leveraging the reasoning ability of multi-modal large language model (MLLM), ERIM constructs rule-centric MICL datasets, introduces explicit supervision for rule induction, and fine-tunes MLLM to perform explicit rule-induction via a two-stage training strategy that combines mixed cold-start supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments show consistent performance improvements across diverse MICL settings and demonstrate that correctly inducing underlying rules directly leads to stronger and more stable performance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ERIM 框架：构建以规则为中心的多模态 in-context 数据集，为规则归纳加入显式监督，并用混合冷启动 SFT 加强化学习的两阶段策略微调 MLLM，使其先从示例中归纳规则再作答。
AI.relevance_reason: 把「规则」当作可监督的中间推理状态，可能为 LVR 中轨迹监督方式与从视觉证据中提取任务必要规则提供参照；但其规则以文本显式表达而非 latent 状态生成，迁移可行性需核查。
